correctness.rationale: PASS: For every integer n≥6 and 1≤k≤n−3, the unit-circle Löwner contact criterion is equivalent to nonnegative Fourier moment weights with first two harmonics zero. Reflecting across the deletion-block bisector reduces to E(c)=0, E(c²)=1/2 with extreme cosine values −B and C=cos(π(k+1)/n). The elementary inequality E(c²)≤BC proves impossibility for 3(k+1)>n; conversely the parity-dependent B·C≥1/2 bound and a low-variance adjacent-node distribution bracketing c=0 yield convexly interpolated nonnegative contact weights. This proves global affine-ellipse optimality, not merely circular optimality; every n,k boundary is covered. I independently checked the parity endpoint inequality through n=400 (all passing pairs) and inspected the complete mathematical proof; this finite check corroborates but is not the proof.
